obernants.approximation_semantics: Exact-real model distinguished from deterministic f64 evaluation; finite correspondence only
obernants.assumptions: Declared resource cap, finite inputs and successful allocations
obernants.domain: Finite validated f64 API and separately exact-real target
obernants.observation_scope: Return values, errors, rounded arithmetic and named finite assertions
obernants.operator: Within valid inputs and real candidate outputs, complement contains infeasible or KKT-incompatible pairs and incorrect error outcomes. This is a relational complement of the unique real solution graph, not just a list of negative examples. For the concrete implementation the complement additionally excludes outputs differing from rounded evaluation and includes arithmetic/resource error partitions; real KKT alone is not a full f64 acceptance predicate.

obernants.operator: For fixed r>0 and feasible y, choose any theta; positive coordinates require x_i=y_i+theta, zero coordinates permit x_i<=theta. This nonunique normal-cone fiber includes arbitrary constant shifts. r=0 maps all valid vectors of matching length to zero. Concrete fibers further constrain rounded arithmetic success.

obernants.operator: Each nonempty support S yields theta=(sum_{i in S} x_i-r)/|S|. It is valid exactly when active x_i>theta and inactive x_i<=theta. Exhaustive small support enumeration does not repeat sorting or the prefix scan.

obernants.operator: Real projection is invariant under adding a common constant. Shifting by maximum avoids loss of a small radius against a common large offset; [MAX,MAX] with radius2 yields [1,1]. The subtraction can overflow for mixed extreme signs.

obernants.operator: Radius zero returns all positive zeros after validation, including empty input. Positive radius with empty input is EmptySimplex. Relative mass divides by strictly positive radius; smallest subnormals may be unrepresentable as equal shares and return Arithmetic.
